title: Loop-first pooling controlled false positives in ideal spectral samples from two passive worm models
abstract: We tested two orders of spectral pooling in passive models from two partial adult C. elegans electrical maps. Each experiment used 64 independent blocks, 32 proper complex Gaussian vectors per frequency and nine frequencies. A sign test on loop sines formed before pooling rejected 54 and 61 of 2000 reversible draws with fixed unequal cell filters. Its exact discrete null level was 3.277%. The same test after spectral pooling rejected all 2000 draws in each map. We prove loop-first sign symmetry under joint conjugation invariance and nonzero scalar filters. A directed drift change gave only 6.55% and 4.20% loop-first rejection. Thus null control did not give strong detection at this sample count. Oracle triangle selection, assumed physiology, partial anatomy, independent spectral samples and absent finite-window leakage limit use. No measured activity was tested. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Loop-first and spectrum-first rejection fractions for fixed models. Bars show 95% Wilson Monte Carlo intervals, not animal uncertainty. Dashed line is nominal 5%; the exact discrete null test size is 3.277%.

citations.reason: Extends its population frequency-averaging result to an ideal finite-sample sign test; independent code.
Prior single-frequency power benchmark; this work tests frequency pooling and a different score.
